purpose: Alfuzosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH. It helps relieve problems like difficulty starting urination, a weak urine stream, and the feeling that your bladder never fully empties. It does not shrink the prostate, but it does make urinating much easier and more comfortable.
how_it_works: Your prostate and the muscles around your bladder have special receptors called alpha-1 receptors. When these receptors are activated, those muscles tighten up and make it hard to urinate. Alfuzosin blocks those receptors, which relaxes the muscles in and around your prostate and bladder neck. This relaxation allows urine to flow more freely and easily.
common_side_effects: Dizziness or lightheadedness, especially when you stand up quickly. Headache, tiredness, or feeling run down. Stuffy or runny nose. Stomach upset or nausea. These effects are usually mild and often improve after the first few days.
warnings: This medication can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure when you stand up, which may make you feel dizzy or faint — especially after your first dose. Take it with food and at bedtime to lower this risk. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor or dentist you take this drug before any surgery, especially eye surgery, as it can affect eye muscles. Do not take it with certain blood pressure medications or other alpha-blockers without your doctor's approval. Men should also be aware it can rarely cause a prolonged, painful erection — seek medical help right away if that happens.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 10 mg extended-release tablet taken by mouth once a day, always with the same meal each day — usually your evening meal. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or cut it. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep a steady level in your body.
